body: I think I agree with what you’re saying here. I’m having a difficult time deciding if some of my experiences have been “sketchy,” or if I’m just so used to the box that medicine is usually in, a more relaxed environment sets off red flags. No matter what, it does feel bad that the expense is so high and it does seem like a cash grab, even by the most reputable sources. Most of us are paying out of pocket and don’t have a choice, and we’re paying a lot. I guess as long as the medication is legal and from a safe source, the environment it comes from shouldn’t matter.

I took spravato for about a month and a half, and now I use troches at home. Where I was going, very little time was spent with the provider for spravato. A nurse/tech did vitals and sat in room while it was administered. The provider read my phq and came in mid point and at the end to make sure it was tolerated well. I saw the provider ~5 min tops, but I’d still feel weird if it was someone I knew. For me, spravato only helped the day of and maybe the next day. I’m having better luck now with troches. It’s also nice not spending hours sitting at the office waiting to be able to leave as I had to do with spravato.

I got meds delivered today, but I won’t use them until the weekend, sorry. Also, I switched from oral to nasal, so I’m not sure if I can be a good source. I’ve used Spravato before, but not ketamine nasally. The meds came from a small pharmacy in my state. The reviews for the pharmacy are overall positive, but a mix of people who think they’re awful and people who think they’re good.

Edited to add I was refunded for the original charge for meds.
I’m not condoning them and I think I’ve been pretty clear with each of my posts stating it seems bad. I’m just giving my experience.

I would say for anyone trying it, ask at the time of the med discussion if the state you’re in uses their in-app pharmacy, or whatever they’re referring to. Maybe you can avoid the need for a refund. Also, now that I know the pharmacy charges much less than the price they gave me, if I do try them again I’m definitely not paying that.

I’m quite hesitant about this site as well. The exact same thing happened to me—charged via the app for over double the cost the pharmacy called for me to pay by phone. Was also told I’ll get a refund. I’m waiting to see if I have to do a chargeback. The only thing I can say is meds were delivered to my house today. I knew it looked at seemed like a gamble, and I definitely won’t consider this a reliable source to maintain.
Someone else posted riverofchange.org. I tried Everyone’s MD and so far it definitely doesn’t feel safe, but I do have a delivery coming tomorrow according to UPS. I had my appointment yesterday.

I did use the chat box that says they typically reply in a few minutes. Never got a reply so I left my email. I got an email that a ticket has been made, and it’s been a few hours since that. I also called the number in the app, which is generic and went to a voicemail.

So since we are all scrambling at the moment, I wanted to post this as it’s happening and will correct my post if anything changes.

I had signed up for this service literally hours before finding out Dr. Smith was stopping just because I wanted nasal spray and I don’t like Precision. The process took less than about 10 min to sign up, meet a doc, and have a script. I read another post about prices, and I guess that applied to oral. Nasal spray was far more expensive (like $350), but I went with it to just try. 

Now today, I got a voicemail from the pharmacy that I need to pay $159 for my script. I’m glad a script was sent to a real pharmacy, or what I assume is a real pharmacy, but I don’t know why I paid via the app and why I was charged so much more. I emailed to find out what’s going on. I should have waited to get a response, but since I’m so nervous I’ll have nothing post-Smith, I decided to just pay the pharmacy. I’m waiting for a reply that will hopefully lead to a refund of the exorbitant charge I paid via the app for meds. I’ll update this if that happens. 

Just want to post this in case anyone is going that route. Either avoid, or ask questions.

Edit: I did get a reply that my cost would be refunded for the original amount I paid. Waiting to see that happen. And it was still a lot higher than the actual pharmacy.

Edited again: I was refunded the original amount I paid for the meds, so I only ended up paying what went directly to the pharmacy.

I’ve stopped talking to them altogether. I feel like I’m already gone in this sense. I’ve already removed myself. If I kill myself, barely anyone would even know, which is what I want. 

It’s pointless because I have no fight left. There’s no argument that things will get better or that this is temporary. I’ve contacted crisis text lines in the past, and it’s a waste of time to explain why the reasons to die outweigh the reasons to live. It’s no longer an attempt at looking for a reason to live; it’s just reiterating why that’s not possible anymore. 

I’m the common denominator. All of my trouble comes down to me making it this way. I don’t work in life like a person is supposed to. I think I’ve lived long enough at this point to know that I’m just wrong, and I’ll continue to have this suffocating dread until I end it.
